references.text: God's promise to Abraham that in him all the families of the earth would be blessed – the same promise renewed to Jacob with almost identical wording.
God promises Abraham to look in every direction and that his descendants will become like the dust of the earth (כַּעֲפַר הָאָרֶץ), the same expression and motif repeated in the promise to Jacob.
The promise that in Abraham's offspring all the nations of the earth would be blessed, the same promise renewed to Jacob.
The promise to Isaac of numerous descendants and that all the nations of the earth would be blessed in his offspring – continued to his son Jacob.
Paul refers to the promise given to Abraham that in his offspring all nations would be blessed, a promise that was renewed to Jacob.
Peter quotes the promise that all the families of the earth will be blessed in Abraham's offspring, with wording that directly reflects Genesis 28:14.
A direct parallel in Abraham's covenant where 'the dust of the earth' is used as a metaphor for an endlessly numerous offspring.
A strong thematic parallel in the geographical expansion and conquest of land as fulfillment of Abraham's promise.
